features.name: Proofreading quality
features.description: Captures how carefully edited and error-free the letter is, which affects professionalism and confidence in detail-sensitive security work.

levels.descriptor: Frequent spelling or typographical errors distract from the content and suggest weak attention to detail.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the overall message remains understandable.
The letter is mostly clean, with only minor slips that do not materially hurt credibility.
The writing is polished and essentially error-free throughout.

features.name: Role-specific motivation
features.description: Captures how specifically and convincingly the letter explains why this exact security automation role fits the applicant's interests and goals.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific motivation beyond wanting a software job or a brand-name employer.
Mentions security, scale, or Google in broad terms without a strong personal rationale.
Gives a clear role-relevant reason for interest, such as secure-by-default tooling or scaling scarce security effort.
Presents a precise, memorable thesis for wanting this role that is tightly tied to the team's mandate and the applicant's own priorities.

features.evidence: improvements there are inherited by every team downstream
features.name: Platform leverage mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant values internal infrastructure whose impact comes from enabling many other teams rather than owning a single product surface.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or multiplatform work.
Makes only a brief nod to broad impact or company scale.
Clearly appreciates tooling or infrastructure that benefits many engineers or services.
Consistently frames past work and future goals in terms of inherited leverage across an organization.

features.evidence: 5 years at Microsoft launching 6 production services
features.name: Delivery depth
features.description: Captures the amount of relevant professional software delivery experience shown through years of work and repeated production launches or ownership.

levels.descriptor: Shows only minimal or weakly substantiated production software experience.
Shows a few years of relevant work with some concrete production maintenance or launch experience.
Shows solid multi-year experience with repeated ownership of several production services.
Shows extensive relevant delivery history across many years and multiple production systems.

features.evidence: Master's degree or Doctoral degree in computer science
features.name: Academic preparation
features.description: Captures the strength of formal academic credentials relative to the role's preference for advanced technical study.

levels.descriptor: No clearly relevant degree or equivalent preparation is provided.
Shows a relevant bachelor's degree or comparable practical preparation.
Shows a relevant master's degree or similarly advanced formal study.
Shows a relevant doctoral degree or unusually strong advanced research preparation.

features.evidence: Python is production-grade, not just scripting
features.name: Python production depth
features.description: Captures how much real production ownership the letter shows with Python rather than merely naming it.

levels.descriptor: Provides no meaningful Python evidence.
Mentions Python briefly or only as light scripting experience.
Shows regular production use of Python for services, tooling, automation, or internal systems.
Shows deep production-grade Python experience, such as typed and tested services, broad organizational tooling, or code other engineers extend confidently.

features.evidence: LLM-based features that had to behave predictably in production
features.name: AI production rigor
features.description: Captures whether AI experience is absent, merely fashionable, or shown as production work with reliability and evaluation concerns.

levels.descriptor: Shows no AI experience.
Mentions AI interest or exposure without clear production responsibility.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality in production.
Shows production AI experience plus explicit evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or reliability engineering.

features.evidence: Python agents with Go services defining permissions and audit
features.name: Agentic architecture ownership
features.description: Captures the extent to which the applicant has designed agent-based systems with explicit control boundaries rather than only mentioning AI generally.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention agentic systems.
Mentions agents or pipelines but gives little design detail.
Describes building end-to-end agentic tooling with Python agents and Go back-end services.
Shows deliberate agentic architecture choices such as permissions, bounded actions, auditing, decomposition, or guardrails.

features.evidence: classified, deduplicated, and routed vulnerability reports
features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience automating the intake and handling of vulnerability reports, which is central to the role.

levels.descriptor: Shows no evidence of vulnerability handling automation.
Expresses interest in vulnerability response or mentions vague automation without a clear example.
Describes building tooling or pipelines to automate vulnerability report triage.
Shows concrete triage mechanics or impact, such as classification, deduplication, routing, variant handling, or measured workload reduction.

features.evidence: threat modeling and code review for common vulnerability classes
features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues beyond general secure coding claims.

levels.descriptor: Provides no meaningful security assessment evidence.
Suggests security review interest but without a clear assessment method or scope.
Shows clear assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, or service reviews.
Shows structured assessment practice with attack-surface analysis, formal findings, validation of fixes, or repeated cross-service assessment ownership.

features.evidence: replaced ad-hoc traversals with proper graph algorithms
features.name: Algorithmic sophistication
features.description: Captures whether the letter demonstrates active use of data structures and algorithms to solve difficult systems problems.

levels.descriptor: Provides no evidence of data structure or algorithmic strength.
Claims algorithmic strength but gives little or no concrete example.
Gives a specific redesign or performance example that shows practical algorithmic skill.
Shows a particularly crisp algorithmic intervention tied to a hard production problem and a meaningful improvement.

features.evidence: near-top finishes in several big capture-the-flag events
features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures how actively the applicant sharpens adversarial thinking through exercises such as capture-the-flag competitions.

levels.descriptor: Mentions no offensive security practice.
Mentions casual or occasional practice without evidence of sustained engagement.
Shows regular offensive practice presented as ongoing skill maintenance.
Shows serious offensive practice with strong results, high commitment, or both.

features.name: Security credential
features.description: Captures the strength of formal security certification evidence included in the letter.

levels.descriptor: Lists no security credential.
Lists a baseline credential, such as Security+ or a similar fundamentals-level certification.
Lists a stronger practical credential, such as OSCP, without much supporting detail.
Lists a strong practical credential and frames it with hands-on exploitation or similarly rigorous validation.

features.evidence: maintainer of an actively used open-source project
features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures whether the applicant simply consumes open source, occasionally patches it, or actively maintains software used by others.

levels.descriptor: Mentions no open-source contribution.
Mentions occasional patches or upstream fixes.
Shows regular contributions or maintenance of a small project or library.
Shows clear stewardship of an actively used open-source project, including reviews, releases, or community support.

features.evidence: distributed task queue with exactly-once semantics
features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical scope and seriousness of independent projects used to demonstrate engineering depth outside work.

levels.descriptor: Mentions no personal project.
Mentions only a small utility or routine application.
Shows a substantial side project with meaningful systems design or operational complexity.
Shows an ambitious project tackling difficult reliability, distributed-systems, or low-level engineering problems to a high standard.

features.evidence: measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned
features.name: Achievement concreteness
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter describes accomplishments, mechanics, and outcomes rather than relying on generic self-claims.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on generic claims with little evidence of what was actually built or achieved.
Provides some concrete facts, but mechanics and outcomes remain thin.
Gives several specific examples showing what was built and why it mattered.
Provides richly concrete accomplishments with clear mechanisms, stakes, and impact.
